title: Regret now, regret later
hook: Would your worst regret change if we asked next year?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish short-term action regret from longer-term inaction regret.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish short-term action regret from longer-term inaction regret.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: In a toy regret rule, a loss of ten receives action weight 0.8 and inaction weight 0.2. What action-regret score results? Toy inputs A=[10, 0.8]; B=[10, 0.2].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[8, 1.9999999999999996, 6.000000000000001], [2, 8, -6]]. Labels: Action regret, Inaction regret, Gap.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Changing the weighting rule reverses which kind of regret dominates without changing the loss. These are explicit toy weights; they illustrate how a time-dependent comparison could work, not a universal emotional response.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Loss units=10, Action weight=0.2. What is Action regret? Answer: 2.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Loss units=10, Action weight=0.2. What is Action regret?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 2. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Actions are regretted more in the short run (Kahneman & Tversky, 1982), but inactions more over a lifetime (Gilovich & Medvec, 1995).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish short-term action regret from longer-term inaction regret.
